To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) investment is sensitive to permanent technology shocks, (2) cash flow and Tobin's Q respond to both permanent and temporary shocks, (3) the gestation lag is about 12 quarters, and (4) the marginal q for investment is the expected value of future cash flow discounted at the marginal cost of capital.

In summary, our research is concerned with
the question of why investment does not always occur when cash flow or Tobin's q is high and why it does not always occur quickly.
the gestation lags that arise when investment is subject to planning and building delays.
the role of gestation delays in investment decisions.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the investment decision is not made at the time when capital becomes productive.
the gestation lag for capital is about 8 quarters.
the gestation lag is a major factor in explaining investment behavior.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the gestation lag is a major source of noise for investment, cash flow, and q.
investment is not a function of Tobin's Q or cash flow.
the gestation lag is a key feature of investment that has been overlooked by many researchers.
The main takeaway from our work is that
investment is a long and uncertain process.
the gestation lag is an important determinant of the investment process.
investment is more sensitive to permanent shocks than to temporary shocks and more sensitive to technology shocks than to demand shocks.
